summary.headline: Nirlon Q1 FY27: total income Rs.173 crore (+3% YoY), EBITDA Rs.134 crore (+1%), PAT about Rs.69 crore (+19%), occupancy 99.8%.
summary.overview: Nirlon reported Q1 FY27 total income of about Rs.173 crore (+3% YoY), EBITDA of Rs.134 crore (+1% YoY, 77.30% margin) and PAT of about Rs.69 crore (+19% YoY, 40.19% margin). Average occupancy across NKP and Nirlon House was 99.8%, with about 6,900 sq ft vacant at June 30, 2026. Management said FY27 is a quiet year for lease expiries and rental growth will come mainly from contracted escalations; no tenant additions were made in the quarter. On REIT conversion, Nirlon House redevelopment and GIC-related talks, management gave no new substantive update.

financial_highlights.change: Management described it as moderating sequentially per analyst; no YoY figure stated

segments.name: NKP (Nirlon Knowledge Park)
segments.commentary: Operating leases are fully contracted; management expects no significant new additions in Q1 FY27 and no major lease expiries in FY27. Routine capex only for upgrades to Grade A standard.

segments.name: Nirlon House
segments.commentary: Leased about 1,100 sq ft office in Q1 at roughly Rs.250 per sq ft per month (analyst's figure; management confirmed approx). Building has 12 other co-owners, so redevelopment needs their consent and no update was given.

guidance_outlook: Rental growth for rest of FY27 to come predominantly from contracted escalations under existing leave and licence agreements; no significant growth outside contracts expected.
Annual escalations of about 4.75% (plus or minus a few basis points), replacing the earlier 15% every three years structure.
EBITDA margins expected to stay steady, based on existing contracts; management hopes to maintain and improve them.
Debt repayment starts May 2027: 5% per year, totalling 25%, under the existing lender agreement.
Management declined to guide on FY27 dividend or on net debt trajectory (analyst asked about moving to about 1.5 from 1.8).
No decision on prepaying debt; no serious discussion with lenders yet.
capex_capacity: Only routine capex planned at NKP for upgrades and maintenance to keep the park at international Grade A standard; no redevelopment or expansion announced.
No new capacity or commissioning timelines were disclosed.
demand_pricing: Management says occupancy is essentially full, so live or serious inquiries are few; demand is going elsewhere in the Goregaon/western suburbs micro market.
Management views rentals as competitive but declined to compare them with other Goregaon assets, citing differences in efficiency, rent-free periods, deposits and escalations.
GCC growth described as a positive driver of Mumbai and Maharashtra office demand; no quantified data given.
Old-building carpet-to-chargeable efficiency at Nirlon House about 95-100%.

qa_highlights.question: Any plan to convert to a REIT, given the tax amendment for REIT dividends?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there are no concrete plans to convert to a REIT and it will disclose any significant structural change.

qa_highlights.question: Any progress on redeveloping Nirlon House?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said redevelopment needs consent from 12 other co-owners, takes significant time, and there is nothing significant to report.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company prepay debt given healthy cash?
qa_highlights.answer: No decision has been taken and no serious discussion has happened with lenders on prepayment.

qa_highlights.question: How should rental growth look for the rest of FY27, and are there lease expiries?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth will follow contracts; FY27 is described as a fairly quiet year with no significant expiries and nothing heard from larger licensees to suggest otherwise.

qa_highlights.question: Why did licence-fee income grow only 0.9% QoQ, and will EBITDA margins hold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed this to contracted licences with escalations timing; it hopes margins hold, expecting only steady fluctuation based on contracts.

qa_highlights.question: What is the dividend outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 dividend rose to Rs.30 per share from Rs.26, but it would not comment on FY27 dividend, which has not been discussed internally.

qa_highlights.question: Net debt trajectory and restructuring progress?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to speculate on net debt numbers and said there is nothing significant to report on GIC or Nirlon House talks.

risks_watch: Growth is capped by fully contracted, nearly full occupancy; no new leasing upside visible in FY27.
Debt amortisation starts May 2027 (5% a year, 25% total), which may affect EBITDA margins and leverage; the analyst cited net debt of 1.81.
No dividend guidance for FY27 after the Rs.30 FY26 payout; watch for the interim and final dividend announcements.
Nirlon House redevelopment and REIT conversion remain unresolved; co-owner consent needed.
Licence-fee growth slowed to 0.9% QoQ; the next quarter will show whether escalations flow through.
Management gave no ETA for an average remaining lease tenure figure, which was withheld on the call.
summary.management_tone: Confident on occupancy and contracted rentals but noticeably cautious and evasive on forward items: REIT, Nirlon House, GIC talks, dividend, net debt and lease tenure all got non-committal answers.
key_quotes: As of right now, to answer your question very frankly, there is nothing very significant to say.

So, basically, we of course are trying to get as much information and details, etc., with regards to GCCs, because GCCs, as you know, are a very good source, are a very important source of real estate demand in Mumbai, Maharashtra, as well as in India.
26-27 is a fairly quiet year in terms of any significant leave and license agreements expiring or getting off in terms of any of the existing leave and license agreements expiring.
